summary.headline: Afcom Q4 FY26 revenue rose 87.8% YoY to INR191.88 crore and PAT to INR44.66 crore, on war-driven charter demand.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR191.88 crore (+87.8% YoY), EBITDA of INR74.08 lakh per the call (+51.52%), and PAT of INR44.66 crore (+72.85%) under Ind AS. Full-year revenue was INR587.72 crore (+143.86%) and PAT INR121.90 crore (+230.05%), with PAT margin of 20.74%. Growth was driven by stranded-cargo charters after Middle East disruption in March 2026, with 415 of 602 Q4 trips being pure charters. Fleet expansion is the key near-term constraint: a third aircraft is operational, with fourth and fifth expected before the next quarter and wide-bodies (Boeing 777) planned from late 2026.

financial_highlights.change: +72.85% YoY; GAAP PAT was INR46.32 crore

segments.name: Dry lease (aircraft-plus-crew charter/scheduled cargo)
segments.commentary: Q4 dry lease revenue INR160.49 crore; FY26 INR528.71 crore on 1,923 trips and 24,353 tons, with 1,129 pure charters (about one-third in Q4).

segments.name: Q4 operating metrics
segments.commentary: Q4 average revenue per trip USD29,295.64 and yield USD2.72/kg versus FY yield USD2.54/kg; cost per kg USD1.84 in Q4 versus USD1.58 for FY. Weekly trips per aircraft averaged 23.42 in Q4 and 19 for FY.

guidance_outlook: Fourth and fifth Boeing 737-type aircraft expected to be operational before the next quarter (Q1 FY27), per management.

Two Boeing 777 wide-body aircraft: one expected operational in the last quarter of FY27 (per the call's timing), with the full four-777 plan expected to be fully operational by mid/second half of calendar 2027.

Management called a 777 revenue of about 3x a 737-800 at 14-15 rotations/month and 75% load factor, implying roughly INR75 crore/month per 777 as a conservative estimate; management said FY27 revenue could be at least double FY26 on existing resources.
ATF pass-through via fuel surcharge; designated carrier status cuts fuel-related VAT, adding about 5-7% benefit to overall fuel cost from the next financial year.
Maintenance reserve now expensed to P&L under Ind AS; management says no further fundraise needed for the fleet plan after QIB and preferential issues.
capex_capacity: Three aircraft in operation: VT-AFO, VT-AFN and the newly inducted third aircraft (VT-AFJ per Q&A), with the third aircraft held for a fresh C-check and contracted Middle East flying from late June.

FY26 capacity utilisation 81.42% on gross weight basis; utilisation hours per aircraft per day peaked at 11.45 (VT-AFO) and 10.51 (VT-AFN) in Q4 versus industry best 10-14 hours and Asia Pacific average 7.9.
Lease-related liability: three aircraft ROU assets INR306 crore, total lease liability INR338 crore, current lease dues INR49 crore plus INR16.1 crore lease finance cost over 12 months.

Funding: QIB and preferential allotment (INR200 crore each per analyst) stated to cover wide-body induction; fourth and fifth aircraft costs largely covered, with customs and minor expenses remaining.
demand_pricing: March 2026 saw a sudden capacity withdrawal from Middle East carriers; Q4 month-end revenue ran about INR42-44 crore per month, with March about 22-23% above the Jan-Feb average.

Management said April and May demand remained above average but below March panic levels; fuel prices (ATF) at INR2,24,000/KL were offered at INR1,69,000/KL under designated carrier status, versus INR85,000/KL before.
Q4 yield USD2.72/kg versus IATA industry average cited at INR222/kg; management said company yield per kg is better than the IATA average.
Chennai international cargo grew 12.5% YoY in FY26 versus 5.4% all-India, per management's data.
Over 60% of billing is in USD. Receivables about 60 days on recent billing (IATA norm 45 days); management said no receivables older than 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for fourth, fifth and wide-body aircraft induction?
qa_highlights.answer: Third aircraft operational; fourth and fifth to be operational before next quarter; one 777 targeted in last quarter of FY27, with four 777s in total per management's later clarification, fully operational by second half of calendar 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of ATF price surge and pass-through to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fuel is passed through 100% via fuel surcharge; the market absorbed the April spike, which tapered in May and June; designated carrier status yields a fuel price benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 yield only USD2.72/kg despite higher freight rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher charter share (415 of 602 Q4 trips) and short-sector stranded-cargo flights lowered yield per kg; more weight-based cargo would have raised yield.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential of 777 aircraft?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 777 can do 14-15 rotations per month at 75% load factor, giving about 3x a 737-800's revenue; an analyst's estimate of about INR75 crore per month per 777 was described as conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 EBITDA margin lower than Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to Ind AS adjustments, particularly a large forex loss charged to P&L, and maintenance reserve now expensed.

qa_highlights.question: Ideal FY27 revenue expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said resources would at least double FY26 revenue on a conservative basis; no numerical guidance given.

risks_watch: Fuel price volatility (ATF up sharply from April) and dependence on a fuel surcharge pass-through; pricing could soften if the Middle East disruption ends.
Revenue dependence on temporary war-driven charter demand; management acknowledged yields hardened in March and the sea-freight alternative is also rising in cost.
Ind AS restatement now shows large forex losses and maintenance reserve charges, which compress reported margins; Q4 EBITDA margin lower than Q3.
Tax liability: about INR33 crore of FY26 current tax outstanding per analyst; management acknowledged only partial advance tax payment and promised improvement.
Aircraft induction delays (fourth, fifth and 777 timelines) and third aircraft utilisation; aircraft tracking data disputed by management.
Disclosure gaps: cargo-type revenue breakdown (ODC, general, hazardous, perishables) and Nauru JV/MRO details not provided pending UPSI considerations.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, fleet expansion and the war-driven demand, but evasive on specifics such as 777 routes, Nauru details and timelines, citing UPSI and sensitivity; some answers were inconsistent on aircraft counts and dates.
key_quotes: Q4 was one of the best, in the journey of AFCOM so far.
Sir, the demand is high, we are short of capacity. And every aircraft that comes, every kg of capacity that we put in will be fully utilized.
In our industry fuel cost is a direct pass-on to the end customer.
So we don't require any further, you know, the fundraise, you know, for the fleet expansion whatever we have envisaged and communicated.

adds.what: Boeing 777 wide-body aircraft (two in plan; one expected in last quarter of FY27, four-777 plan fully operational by mid/H2 CY27)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue to at least double FY26 (about 100%+ growth, unquantified), backed by fleet induction of the 4th and 5th 737-type aircraft before Q1 FY27 and 777 wide-bodies later, plus QIB/preferential funding reported as covering the plan; April-May demand stayed above average though below March spike.
